'''Ian Johnston Rhind Aitchison''' (born 1936) is a British physicist and retired academic who was Professor of Physics at the [[University of Oxford]] between 1996 and 2003.

== Career ==
Born in 1936,<ref name="wd2005">''Writers Directory'' ([[St. James Press]], 2005).</ref> Aitchison read mathematics at [[Peterhouse, Cambridge]], graduating with a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in 1958; he then completed a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[theoretical physics]] there in 1961.<ref>[https://www.crcpress.com/authors/i400-ian-aitchison/bio/ "Ian Aitchison"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191203123957/https://www.crcpress.com/authors/i400-ian-aitchison/bio/ |date=3 December 2019 }}, ''CRC Press'' (Taylor & Francis Group). Retrieved 3 December 2019.</ref><ref>''The Cambridge University List of Members Up to 31 December 1988'' (Cambridge University Press, 1989), p. 11.</ref>

Between 1961 and 1963, Aitchison was a research associate at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] in [[New York (state)|New York]], United States; after a year at the [[Saclay Nuclear Research Centre]] in [[France]], he worked as a research associate at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] from 1964 to 1966. In 1966, he was elected a [[fellow]] of [[Worcester College, Oxford]], and appointed a university [[lecturer]] in theoretical physics; he was [[Titles of Distinction awarded by the University of Oxford|awarded the title]] of [[Professor]] of Physics in 1996 and retired in 2003. He remains an [[emeritus]] professor at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="wd2005" /><ref>[http://www.ox.ac.uk/media/global/wwwoxacuk/localsites/gazette/documents/universitycalendar/EMERITUS.pdf "Professors Emeritus"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130425162146/http://www.ox.ac.uk/media/global/wwwoxacuk/localsites/gazette/documents/universitycalendar/EMERITUS.pdf |date=25 April 2013 }}, ''Oxford University Calendar''. Retrieved 3 December 2019.</ref>

== Bibliography ==

* ''Relativistic Quantum Mechanics'' ([[Macmillan Publishers|Macmillan]], 1972).
* (Co-editor with Jack E. Paton) ''Rudolf Peierls and Theoretical Physics: Proceedings of the symposium held in Oxford on July 11th & 12th, 1974, to mark the occasion of the retirement of Professor Sir Rudolph E. Peierls, F.R.S., C.B.E.'' ([[Pergamon Press]], 1977). {{isbn|0-08-020606-9}} hbk.
* (Co-authored with [[Tony Hey|A. J. G. Hey]]) ''Gauge Theories in Particle Physics'' (1st ed. [[Adam Hilger|Hilger]] and [[University of Sussex Press]], 1982; 2nd ed. 1989; 3rd ed. [[Taylor & Francis|Taylor and Francis]], 2002; [https://books.google.com/books?id=jIoTEAAAQBAJ 4th ed., vols. 1 & 2] [[CRC Press]], 2012; 5th ed., vols. 1 & 2 [[CRC Press]], 2024).
* ''An Informal Introduction to Gauge Field Theories'' ([[Cambridge University Press]], 1982; reprinted with corrections, 1984; digitally printed with additional corrections, 2007).
* (Co-editor with [[Christopher Llewellyn Smith|C. H. Llewellyn Smith]] and [[Jack Paton (physicist)|J. E. Paton]]) ''Plots, Quarks and Strange Particles: Proceedings of the Dalitz Conference 1990'' ([[World Scientific]], 1991).
* ''Supersymmetry in Particle Physics: An Elementary Introduction'' ([[Cambridge University Press]], 2007). {{isbn|9781139467056}}
